value.answer: This sounds like a common viral stomach bug in toddlers - it usually runs its course in a few days. Good signs you're already seeing: taking fluids okay and steady wet diapers. Keep offering small, frequent sips (water, milk, or an oral rehydration drink) and regular food as tolerated. Watch for: no urine in 8+ hours, very sleepy or hard to wake, sunken eyes, no tears, dry mouth, blood in stool/vomit, high fever, or belly pain that won't ease.
value.triage: Call Health811 if fluids get harder to keep down, diarrhea/vomiting drags past 3-5 days, or you're unsure about dehydration. Go to the ER or call 911 now if there's no wet diaper in 8+ hours, sunken eyes/no tears, lethargy or trouble waking, blood in vomit or stool, or signs of severe dehydration.
value.sources: HealthyChildren.org (AAP), CDC - Diarrhea in Children, Caring for Kids (CPS)
